cases.setup: Provide a pinned public Rust checkout with a reproduction and a dispatcher that admits an asynchronous context-manager statement to a rule omitting that variant.
checks: The report identifies current dispatcher, rule and regression owner bindings with hashed anchors.
The report names both the admitted asynchronous variant and the absent rule match arm.
The report records the synchronous context-manager extraction and body traversal used as the repair anchor.
Tracked file hashes remain unchanged after inspection.
Only confirmed current evidence produces the mismatch-confirmed output port.

cases.setup: Provide current anchors where both context-manager variants are already handled and the panic comes from a different expression traversal.
checks: No mismatch-confirmed output is emitted.
The observation records a mechanism mismatch rather than recommending the historical edit.
No tracked source or expectation file changes.

cases.setup: Provide confirmed mismatch evidence, compatible Rust statement variants, bound owners and editable public regression fixtures.
checks: The diff routes synchronous and asynchronous context-manager statements through the existing binding extraction and body traversal.
The statement-only rule signature and all changed callers are consistent.
The fallback still rejects genuinely unsupported statements rather than suppressing all failures.
The public regression fixture contains reused-name and distinct-name asynchronous context-manager cases and retained asynchronous-loop reuse coverage.
Expected diagnostics identify the inner reused binding and omit the distinct-name control.
Existing loop, assignment, target-comparison and scope-boundary logic is not removed.
Any previous public-validation-observed fact is marked stale after the edit.

cases.setup: Provide the post-edit state, reviewed public expected outputs and current-bound reproduction and repository-test argv commands; disable automatic snapshot acceptance.
checks: The original no-as asynchronous context-manager reproduction completes without panic or a binding-redefinition diagnostic.
The reused-name asynchronous context-manager case emits the diagnostic at the inner target.
The distinct-name control emits no binding-redefinition diagnostic.
Asynchronous-loop reuse and existing synchronous context-manager, loop, assignment, unpacking and nested-scope assertions retain their behavior.
Changed rule and dispatch callers compile through the public harness.
Tracked expected outputs are not silently regenerated during verification.
The report records actual command outcomes and PASS, FAIL or UNKNOWN for every bound oracle.
A failing or unknown required oracle does not authorize repair acceptance.
